The test image shows a corn husk/ear with:
- Brownish-tan husk discoloration
- Dark/black fungal masses or sooty spots on the husk surface
- Reddish-brown water-soaked streaking along the tissue

Top candidates: **Ear_rots_Gibberella** (dark black perithecia on husks with reddish-brown streaking) or **Goss_wilt** (dark exudate freckles on leaf tissue).

Let me view reference images for the top candidates:

The Gibberella reference images are an excellent match — showing husks with dark black sooty perithecia masses and brown-reddish-tan water-soaked discoloration, exactly like the test image. Goss_wilt doesn't match (it affects leaves with bacterial exudate freckles).

Let me view a few more reference images to be thorough:
Diplodia shows white cottony mycelium (no match), SCLB shows discrete leaf lesions (no match). The test image is clearly a husk with dark perithecia masses — Gibberella remains the strongest match.

Neither Anthracnose_stalk_rot (stalk internodes with shiny black rind) nor Tar_spot (small discrete raised black dots on leaf blades) match the test image.

## Analysis Summary

**Test image features:**
- Corn **husk/ear** tissue (not leaf blade or stalk)
- Brownish-reddish-tan, water-soaked discoloration across the husk
- **Dark black sooty masses** scattered and smeared on husk surface — characteristic perithecia
- Papery, dried husk texture with longitudinal streaking

**Why Ear_rots_Gibberella:**
- The Gibberella reference images show an almost identical pattern: husk and leaf sheaths with brown-to-reddish-tan discoloration **streaked with dark black sooty perithecia masses** — exactly matching the test image
- The dark black patches in the test image correspond precisely to the fungal spore masses (perithecia) described as "scattered black specks or smeared streaks along the vascular tissue" on husks
- No white cottony mycelium (rules out Diplodia), no olive-green powder (rules out Aspergillus), no blue-green growth (rules out Trichoderma), no pink coloration (the pink/red in Gibberella is on kernels; husk presentation matches here)
